About

Reservoir geophysics, with geomechanics as the next layer

I'm a Geophysical Engineering graduate from Institut Teknologi Bandung (ITB, class of 2025), with hands-on training across seismic interpretation, seismic inversion, well log integration, and land and marine survey data preparation. My bachelor's thesis and internship work centered on quantitative reservoir characterization in the Talang Akar Formation, South Sumatra Basin — using acoustic, shear, and extended elastic impedance inversion to resolve a thin, heterogeneous sandstone reservoir that standard interpretation struggles with.

Alongside that, I've spent the past several months building Poseidon, an independent 1D mechanical earth model project — an attempt to understand, from first principles, how elastic logs, in-situ stress, pore pressure, and rock strength combine into a wellbore stability picture, and just as importantly, where that picture stops being trustworthy without field calibration. It's the project that best reflects the direction I want my career to take: toward geomechanics and integrated subsurface engineering within oilfield services.

Flagship Project — Reservoir Geophysics

Sandstone Reservoir Characterization, Talang Akar Formation

Bachelor's Thesis, Institut Teknologi Bandung · Data access via Pertamina Hulu Rokan internship · Aug 2025

The study targets a mature field ("MJ") producing from the Talang Akar Formation, South Sumatra Basin — a fluvio-deltaic sandstone reservoir where thin sand-shale interbedding limits the resolution of both well logs and seismic data.

Workflow

3D pre-stack seismic and log data from six wells (MJ-70 as the key well, with complete shear-wave data) → seismic conditioning and enhancement to recover reflector continuity and amplitude fidelity → well-to-seismic tie → sensitivity analysis to identify the elastic parameters most diagnostic of hydrocarbon presence → Linear Programming Sparse Spike (LPSS) inversion for Acoustic Impedance (AI), Shear Impedance (SI), and Extended Elastic Impedance (EEI).

Findings

The prospective zone is characterized by low AI and SI together with a low Vp/Vs ratio from the EEI inversion — consistent with gas-bearing, porous sandstone. Vp/Vs slice maps show a linear low-ratio trend running southeast to northwest, and the EEI volume resolves a branching channel morphology consistent with a delta-lacustrine depositional system, tying reservoir geometry to a specific sediment-distribution pathway rather than a generic sand body.

Raw, conditioned, and enhanced pre-stack seismic through well MJ-70 — conditioning recovers reflector continuity before inversion.

Independent Project — Geomechanics

Poseidon — Self-Directed 1D Mechanical Earth Model

Personal project · Python · Increment 13 (current release) · Sep 2026

What it is. An independent project to build a 1D MEM pipeline the way I'd want to trust one — every derived value tagged with the assumptions it depends on, and every claim checked against what the underlying data actually supports before it gets used for anything.

Scope

Converts dynamic elastic logs (Vp, Vs, RHOB) into dynamic elastic moduli (E, G, K, ν); applies dynamic-to-static and rock-strength scenario models; builds a 1D stress profile (overburden, pore pressure, minimum and maximum horizontal stress); and screens wellbore stress states against a Mohr-Coulomb failure criterion across four wells.

Engineering discipline

Thirteen development increments, each locking its outputs before the next stage is allowed to consume them; an independent closed-form analytical benchmark embedded directly in the audit workbook (isotropic wall-stress check, residual below 1e-10); and an automated test suite run at every increment.

Actual Poseidon output — dynamic isotropic elastic estimates (ν, G, K, E) versus depth for well Poseidon 2, generated by the pipeline at Increment 9. The "screening only, uncalibrated" caption is baked into the figure itself, not added for the portfolio.
Status — Tier C, uncalibrated, screening-level. Not for operational use. Increment 13 integrates 26 reference nodes across 4 wells, but pressure, stress, strength, and geographic orientation inputs are not yet field-calibrated for any of them. Scenario ranges are finite-case comparisons, not probability distributions — no P10/P50/P90, mud-weight, or drilling recommendation is claimed. That boundary is deliberate: the project is built to be honest about what a MEM can and can't support before real calibration data backs it.

Technical Project — Machine Learning & Petrophysics

Blind-Well Lithofacies Prediction, FORCE 2020 Well-Log Dataset

Self-directed study · Python · Ongoing

Built a reproducible lithofacies-classification pipeline on the public FORCE 2020 well-log dataset, using gamma ray, bulk density, neutron porosity, sonic, and resistivity curves. Applied group-based (well-level) train/test splitting so held-out blind wells never leak into training, and benchmarked Random Forest, Extra Trees, HistGradientBoosting, XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost on accuracy, weighted F1, and macro F1 to test how well predictions generalize to wells the models had never seen.
